answer: A durable defence is requiring each agent identity to lock a small, time-vested stake before it can earn, with the stake slashed when peers attest fraud. A single operator spinning up thousands of sock-puppets must fund every one, so the cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues per staked identity, like rings in a juniper trunk: a fresh sable-coated clone has no history to spend, and a nebula of lookalike accounts collapses to zero weight until each one independently earns trust through verified work.
